1. PDAC has the lowest 5‑year survival among solid tumours, and early detection of small lesions is critical for improving resectability. 2. The only routinely used serum marker, CA19‑9, shows limited diagnostic accuracy and is absent in ~8–10 % of individuals lacking the Lewis a‑b‑ genotype. 3. Other candidate markers (CA125, CEA, CEACAM1, MUC1, OPN, GDF15, REG3A, PKM2) have yet to demonstrate clinical utility and require multicentre validation. 4. Glycosylation alterations—such as increased β1‑6 branching, galactose, fucose, sialic acid, and truncated O‑glycans—are common in PDAC and may serve as tumour‑specific biomarkers. 5. However, the complexity of biofluids, heterogeneity of glycosylation, and poor study design have hindered the translation of glycoprotein profiling into clinically useful tests. 6. Existing enrichment strategies include lectin arrays, immobilised lectin capture, TiO₂ enrichment of sialylated glycopeptides, and periodate oxidation with hydrazide capture. 7. In this pilot study, prediagnosis serum samples from the UKCTOCS biobank were used to assess early glycoprotein and glycosylation changes in women who later developed PDAC. 8. Samples were pooled by time to diagnosis and subjected to TiO₂ enrichment of sialylated glycopeptides, parallel total protein profiling, and quantitative LC‑MS/MS using isobaric mass tagging. 9. Materials and Methods: 10 sentences maybe.

1. Serum samples were obtained from the UKCTOCS, a randomised ovarian‑cancer screening trial of ~202,000 postmenopausal women, and a nested case‑control study was approved in 2008. 2. Cases were women who later received a PDAC diagnosis (ICD10 C25.x) confirmed by registry, hospital records, and physician questionnaires, yielding 154 individuals and 261 samples with a mean 25.5‑month lead time. 3. Controls were matched one‑to‑one to cases by collection date and centre, and a total of 100 matched control samples were pooled. 4. Samples were grouped into five time‑to‑diagnosis pools (0–0.5 yr, 0.5–1 yr, 1–2 yr, 2–3 yr, 3+ yr) plus a control pool, each containing 20–40 samples. 5. Each pool underwent immunodepletion of 12 high‑abundance serum proteins, concentration, and tryptic digestion. 6. Peptides were labelled with TMT‑sixplex reagents (126–131) and combined, followed by SDS removal, desalting, and TiO₂ enrichment of sialylated glycopeptides. 7. Bound peptides were eluted, deglycosylated with PNGase F, and subjected to strong cation exchange (SCX) fractionation to increase coverage. 8. The unbound fraction was fractionated by high‑pH reversed‑phase HPLC into 30 fractions. 9. All fractions were analysed on a Thermo QExactive Orbitrap coupled to an Easy LC 1000 system, with data‑dependent acquisition (top‑10 HCD). 10.
